static_traits.name: Qiao Silin
static_traits.family_status: Strong family support, helping each other
static_traits.medical_history: Without major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, capable of self-reflection, highly cooperative, positive attitude; showing significant anxiety when talking about her supervisor and feedback

basic_info.main_problem: I feel ambivalent about my relationship with my supervisor: I dislike him, yet worry about his view of my work ethic. These feelings began a year ago after I took on more responsibilities; they intensify when I make mistakes, and I feel anxious almost daily after interacting with my supervisor or receiving performance feedback, with stress persistently affecting my work performance.
basic_info.core_demands: These ambivalent feelings have affected my mental health and work performance; I feel overwhelmed, so I seek counseling, hoping to relieve anxiety, improve work performance, and view my supervisor's opinion of me more objectively.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on my boss's evaluation

special_situations.event: A supervisor points out his work mistakes in a harsh tone in project feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If criticized or spoken to harshly, it means I am incompetent and not a diligent worker
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to control emotions harder and being doubly careful to avoid repeating mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He thinks I am incompetent / not a diligent person

special_situations.event: When I make a mistake at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake, my boss will think I do not work hard enough; I am just no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-monitoring, working overtime to prove myself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I disappointed him; he will think I am no good

special_situations.event: The boss repeatedly points out mistakes and rarely praises my work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been praised, it means my efforts have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly ruminating on negative feedback, ignoring positive information

special_situations.event: After interacting with supervisor or receiving performance feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only with my supervisor's approval am I a valuable employee
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeks recognition by taking on more tasks and increasing output
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If he does not approve of me, then I have failed

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen by the supervisor, viewed as diligent and competent
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated and seen as incompetent, thus affecting work stability and interpersonal relationships
defense_goal: Avoids criticism and maintains self-worth through doubling effort and self-control

object_relations.self_representation: An employee worried about being negated
object_relations.object_representation: A strict boss who nitpicks and rarely praises

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked by the counselor for evidence and jointly designing a behavioral experiment to test the belief with data
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe that one needs to prove one's own value with facts and data, thereby avoiding directly touching emotional experience
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a calm, rational, structured tone, emphasizing data and facts, minimizing descriptions of subjective feelings.

exception_events.target_problem: When interacting with supervisor or receiving criticism, the client usually thinks the supervisor does not approve of them and develops significant anxiety, followed by decline in work concentration and more mistakes.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On an especially busy night or after completing a complex task, the supervisor recognized her achievements; she noticed that her supervisor does not only see mistakes - her efforts were seen in that specific situation.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different situations and evidence - highly challenging tasks with remarkable results, producing observable positive outcomes; hence positive feedback from the supervisor, breaking the previous dominant narrative of 'only being negated'.

positive_force: Strong family support; willing to confide and gain emotional support
Willing to participate in and carry out behavioral experiments; ample motivation to change
Able to notice evidence that contradicts the negative belief (having been recognized)
negative_force: Prone to mind reading; speculates about the boss's negative views
Mental filtering, over-focusing on negative feedback
Overgeneralization, extending one mistake to overall ability
Excessive reliance on external recognition to determine self-worth

target_behavior.behavior: Significant anxiety and decreased attention when interacting with supervisor or after receiving negative feedback
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being seen as incompetent/not diligent; cognitive distortions (mind reading, overgeneralization, mental filtering) amplify the sense of threat
target_behavior.function: Escaping negative evaluation and potential punishment, trying to reduce mistakes through high vigilance and self-monitoring
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance impaired, more mistakes, tense relationships with colleagues, hard to maintain work-life balance

target_behavior.behavior: Focusing only on negative feedback and ignoring positive information (mental filtering)
antecedent: Lack of immediate praise or recognition
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am not competent enough' and dependence on external recognition make her more sensitive to negative evidence
target_behavior.function: Maintaining the existing self-schema and anticipation consistency, and driving extra effort through self-criticism to seek recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety and self-denial, work engagement and decreased efficiency
